core_obligations: Reduce to the derived limit statement (proof lines 5603-5606): by the general criterion for K-injectivity it suffices to show that the canonical map from the complex to the derived limit of its truncations is an isomorphism.

Apply the companion criterion (proof lines 5606-5607): the vanishing hypothesis of the statement, together with the footnote recording that it may be weakened, is exactly the hypothesis of the companion criterion, which gives the required isomorphism.
proof_roadmap: Use the general criterion to reduce to the derived limit of the truncations.
Apply the companion criterion under the vanishing hypothesis of the statement.
difficulty_reason: The lemma gives conditions under which the canonical map from a complex to the candidate K-injective complex of the section is a quasi-isomorphism, namely a vanishing condition on the cohomology of the cohomology sheaves over a covering family (statement lines 5585-5601, whose standing set-up and displayed equation are delivered verbatim as a context span from lines 5548-5584). The proof reduces the assertion through the general K-injectivity criterion to the statement that the complex is the derived limit of its truncations (proof lines 5603-5606) and then applies the companion criterion of the same section, whose hypothesis is the one appearing in the statement (proof lines 5606-5607). The non-formal content is the reduction through the K-injectivity criterion, and the author additionally records in a footnote that the vanishing hypothesis may be weakened. The claim is H2: a two-step reduction, both steps named.
